verses.1: Having sent Lakshmana away, Rama, filled with sorrow and grief, spoke these words to his chief priest, ministers, and citizens.
verses.2: Rama declared, "Today I shall install the righteous and brave Bharata as the ruler of Ayodhya, and then I myself shall go to the forest."
verses.3: Bring in the preparations, let there be no delay, for today itself I will follow the path that Lakshmana has taken.
verses.4: Having heard those words spoken by Rama, all the subjects greatly bowed their heads to the ground, as if they had lost their very life.
verses.5: Bharata also became unconscious upon hearing Rama's words, and condemning kingship, he spoke these words to Rama.
verses.6: O King, I swear by truth, and indeed by the heavenly world, that I do not desire kingship without you, O delight of the Raghus.
verses.7: O King, O lord of men, enthrone these two, Kusha and Lava; Kusha, the brave, in Kosala, and similarly Lava in the northern regions.
verses.8: Let swift messengers go to Shatrughna and without delay inform him of our departure to heaven.
verses.9: Having heard what Bharata said and seeing the citizens distressed and downcast with sorrow, Vasishtha spoke these words.
verses.10: Vasishtha said, "Dear Rama, behold these subjects fallen to the ground; understanding their desire, do not cause them any displeasure."
verses.11: And by the words of Vasishtha, Rama, having raised up the people, spoke to all, asking, "What shall I do?"
verses.12: Then all the subjects spoke to Rama, saying, "We will follow you, wherever you, Rama, will go."
verses.13: O Rama, if you truly have unsurpassed affection and love for your citizens, then let us all, with our children and wives, accompany you on your path.
verses.14: O Lord, if we are not to be abandoned by you, then lead all of us, whether to a hermitage, a fortress, a river, or the ocean.
verses.15: O King, this is our supreme affection and our greatest wish, for our hearts are always filled with love for following you.
verses.16: Having observed the firm devotion of the citizens and considering his own destined end, Rama said, "Certainly, yes," on that very day.
verses.17: Rama, having consecrated both the brave and great-souled Kusha in Kosala and similarly Lava in the northern regions, completed his arrangements.
verses.18: Then, the mighty-armed Rama, having consecrated his two sons and established them in the city, repeatedly embraced them and kissed them on their heads.
verses.19: He gave to each of his sons thousands of chariots, ten thousands of elephants, and one hundred thousand horses as wealth.
verses.20: He then sent the two brothers, Kusha and Lava, to their respective cities, each endowed with many jewels, much wealth, and surrounded by happy and prosperous people.
verses.21: After consecrating his heroic sons and establishing them in their cities, he then dispatched messengers to the great-souled Shatrughna. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 107 ।। Thus ends the hundred and seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
